reading.body:
CGI is an AI consultant, not an AI builder: it sells strategy, governance, and execution to companies scaling AI, and records no products or MCP servers of its own.

The one concrete engagement in the data is an AI-enabled assessment that accelerated business intelligence migration planning for a large building materials manufacturer. That places CGI on the services side of the AI economy, advising an industrial client rather than supplying compute, buildings, or power. The company's own framing is scale and longevity, a firm grown since 1976 and describing a 50-year milestone and a global culture of ownership.

For AI specifically, this is the layer that sits between the technology and the firms trying to adopt it. Consulting revenue depends on clients deciding to modernize, so it tracks adoption intent rather than the physical constraints of compute and power. Nothing here shows CGI financing, designing, or operating data centers, and no numbers are given for the building materials engagement, so its size and results are unknown.

The data is thin in a specific way. It covers identity, ticker, CIK, and self-description, and it explicitly records no products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers. It cannot say how much of CGI's revenue comes from AI work, how many such engagements exist, or whether the building materials project was completed.
